stem: In a survey, 60% of the respondents were women and the rest were men. Of all the respondents, 45% answered yes to a question. If a man is selected at random from the respondents, the probability that he answered yes is \(0.3\). If a woman is selected at random from the respondents, what is the probability that she answered yes?
solution: Suppose there were 100 respondents: 60 women and 40 men, and \(45\) answered yes.
Men who answered yes: \(0.3 \cdot 40 = 12\). So women who answered yes: \(45 - 12 = 33\).
The probability that a woman answered yes is \(\frac{33}{60} = \frac{11}{20}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(0.45 - 0.3 = 0.15\); the percents cannot simply be subtracted, because they have different bases (all respondents versus men).
explanation.B: Correct. Out of every 100 respondents, 45 said yes, of whom \(0.3 \cdot 40 = 12\) are men, so 33 of the 60 women said yes: \(\frac{33}{60} = \frac{11}{20}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{33}{45}\), the probability that a respondent who answered yes is a woman, not the probability that a woman answered yes.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the overall rate of yes answers, \(45\%\); the rate among women is higher because the men's rate is below the overall rate.

verify:
w, m = 60, 40
yes = 45
my = Rational(3, 10) * m
wy = yes - my
assert (my, wy) == (12, 33)
p = Rational(wy, w)
assert p == Rational(11, 20)
assert value(choices[answer]) == p
assert all(value(choices[k]) != p for k in choices if k != answer)
